es.summary: Trastorno neurodegenerativo progresivo que causa pérdida de memoria, deterioro cognitivo y funcional, y afecta la capacidad de autocuidado.
key_points: Es la causa más frecuente de demencia en adultos mayores
Se caracteriza por placas de beta‑amiloide y ovillos neurofibrilares
El diagnóstico se basa en pruebas neuropsicológicas y neuroimagen
El tratamiento es sintomático: inhibidores de la colinesterasa y memantina
El cuidado integral incluye seguridad, apoyo al cuidador y estimulación cognitiva

pathophysiology: Acumulación de beta‑amiloide forma placas extracelulares
Tau hiperfosforilada genera ovillos neurofibrilares intra‑celulares
Daño sináptico y pérdida neuronal, especialmente en hipocampo y corteza
Reducción de acetilcolina compromete la transmisión cognitiva
signs_symptoms: Pérdida progresiva de memoria a corto plazo
Dificultad para encontrar palabras y seguir conversaciones
Alteraciones del juicio y del razonamiento
Cambios de humor: apatía, irritabilidad, ansiedad
diagnostics: Mini‑Mental State Examination (MMSE) <24 sugiere deterioro cognitivo
Neuropsicología: pruebas de memoria, lenguaje y funciones ejecutivas
Resonancia magnética o TC: atrofia cortical y del hipocampo
Laboratorios: TSH, B12, glucosa para descartar causas reversibles
treatment: Inhibidores de la colinesterasa: donepezilo, rivastigmina, galantamina
Intervenciones no farmacológicas: estimulación cognitiva, ejercicio físico, rutina estructurada
Manejo de comorbilidades: control de presión arterial, glucemia y lípidos
complications: Caídas y fracturas por desorientación y pérdida de equilibrio
Neumonía por aspiración debido a deterioro de la deglución
Incontinencia urinaria y presión de úlceras por inmovilidad
nursing_care: Evaluar nivel de orientación y MMSE en cada turno
Garantizar ambiente seguro: eliminar obstáculos, usar barandillas
Monitorear adherencia a medicación y efectos adversos
Asistir en actividades de la vida diaria según nivel de dependencia
Fomentar comunicación usando preguntas cerradas y recordatorios visuales
patient_teaching: Importancia de tomar los fármacos a la misma hora diariamente
Adaptar el hogar: luces nocturnas, etiquetas en cajones, calendario visible
Promover actividad física ligera y ejercicios de memoria
Educar al cuidador sobre signos de caídas y manejo del estrés

outcomes: Seguridad: sin caídas durante la estancia hospitalaria
Integridad cutánea: sin úlceras por presión al alta

interventions.action: Evaluar entorno y retirar objetos que puedan causar tropiezos
Colocar barandillas en la cama y en el baño
interventions.rationale: Proporciona apoyo físico al paciente desorientado

interventions.action: Enseñar al cuidador técnicas de transferencia segura
Registrar y reportar cualquier episodio de caída o intento de caída
interventions.rationale: Permite intervención temprana y ajuste de medidas de seguridad

outcomes: Ansiedad: nivel de ansiedad ≤3 en escala de 0‑10 al alta
Sueño: paciente reporta dormir ≥6 h sin interrupciones

interventions.action: Crear un ambiente tranquilo con luz tenue y ruido mínimo
interventions.rationale: Disminuye estímulos que aumentan la ansiedad

interventions.action: Practicar técnicas de respiración profunda y relajación guiada
interventions.rationale: Reduce la respuesta fisiológica al estrés

interventions.action: Proveer información clara y sencilla sobre la enfermedad y el plan de cuidados
interventions.rationale: Alivia la incertidumbre y brinda sensación de control

interventions.action: Facilitar la presencia de un cuidador familiar durante la estancia
interventions.rationale: Apoyo emocional disminuye la ansiedad del paciente

en.summary: Progressive neurodegenerative disorder that causes memory loss, cognitive and functional decline, and affects self‑care ability.
key_points: It is the most common cause of dementia in older adults
Characterized by beta‑amyloid plaques and neurofibrillary tangles
Diagnosis is based on neuropsychological tests and neuroimaging
Treatment is symptomatic: cholinesterase inhibitors and memantine
Comprehensive care includes safety, caregiver support, and cognitive stimulation

pathophysiology: Accumulation of beta‑amyloid forms extracellular plaques
Hyperphosphorylated tau generates intracellular neurofibrillary tangles
Synaptic damage and neuronal loss, especially in hippocampus and cortex
signs_symptoms: Difficulty finding words and following conversations
diagnostics: Mini‑Mental State Examination (MMSE) <24 suggests cognitive decline
Neuropsychology: memory, language, executive function tests
MRI or CT: cortical and hippocampal atrophy
Labs: TSH, B12, glucose to rule out reversible causes
treatment: Non‑pharmacologic interventions: cognitive stimulation, physical exercise, structured routine
Managing comorbidities: control blood pressure, glucose, and lipids
complications: Falls and fractures due to disorientation and loss of balance
Aspiration pneumonia due to dysphagia decline
Urinary incontinence and pressure ulcers from immobility
nursing_care: Assess orientation level and MMSE each shift
Ensure a safe environment: remove obstacles, use handrails
Monitor medication adherence and adverse effects
Assist with activities of daily living per dependency level
Encourage communication using closed questions and visual reminders
patient_teaching: Importance of taking medications at the same time daily
Adapt home: night lights, drawer labels, visible calendar
Promote light physical activity and memory exercises
Educate caregiver on fall signs and stress management

outcomes: Safety: no falls during hospital stay
Skin integrity: no pressure ulcers at discharge

interventions.action: Assess environment and remove objects that could cause tripping
Install handrails on bed and in bathroom
interventions.rationale: Provides physical support for disoriented patient

interventions.action: Document and report any fall or fall attempt
interventions.rationale: Allows early intervention and adjustment of safety measures

outcomes: Anxiety: level ≤3 on 0‑10 scale at discharge
Sleep: patient reports ≥6 h uninterrupted sleep

interventions.action: Create a calm environment with dim light and minimal noise
Practice deep breathing and guided relaxation techniques
Provide clear, simple information about the disease and care plan
interventions.rationale: Relieves uncertainty and provides a sense of control

interventions.action: Facilitate presence of a family caregiver during stay

summary.0.quote: The most common form of MND is Alzheimer disease, which is also a neurodegenerative disease , a chronic condition that damages the brain and central nervous system , causing problems with cognitive abilities as well as physical movement.

key_points.0.quote: This disease is the most frequent cause of dementia in older adults .

key_points.1.quote: Current potential causes of AD include: Degeneration of neurons in the hippocampus and cerebral cortex that subsequently cause cerebral atrophy Formation of beta-amyloid plaques Accumulation of neurofibrillary tangles and chemically altered tau protein Oxidative stress forming free radicals that damage cellular components caused by ROS (This is discussed more in the following section.) key_points.3.quote: The medical therapies used for patients with MND may include medications, such as cholinesterase inhibitor s, which can decrease acetylcholine breakdown, enabling nerve cells to communicate; and memantine, which can decrease neurotoxicity (damage to nerve cells) and protect nerve cells from damage.

key_points.4.quote: Two major goals of care are maintaining socialization and providing support for caregivers.
